motivation.title: Motivation
motivation.berlinVotesBody: Every five years Berlin elects a new state parliament (Abgeordnetenhaus) — the body that shapes the city’s policies.
motivation.accessibilityBody: About [16% of German citizens](https://de.statista.com/statistik/daten/studie/1109703/umfrage/bevoelkerung-bezirke-nach-migrationshintergrund-berlin/) in Berlin come from immigrant families. Election programs are only published in German and can run up to 200 pages. That's a hard read even for native speakers. [Wahl-O-Mat](https://www.wahl-o-mat.de/berlin2026/app/main_app.html) helps, but it's not built to go deep.
motivation.clarityBody: Much of the 200 pages is rhetoric, hard to translate into anything concrete. We wanted tangible answers: separating commitments tied to numbers from general statements of intent.
motivation.whatWeDidBody: We compared the positions of 10 Berlin parties on key points across transport, housing, climate and energy, security, education, health, migration, the economy, and democracy — and turned their programs into one side-by-side table.
motivation.beforeYouVoteBody: The table is made with the help of AI; we recommend double-checking points that matter to you. Full translations of the main parties' programs are published on [BerlinVote.Help](https://www.berlinvote.help/).
motivation.furtherReadingIntro: You might also find the following useful:
motivation.furtherReadingBody:
- [Wahl-O-Mat Berlin 2026](https://www.wahl-o-mat.de/berlin2026/app/main_app.html)

about.title: About
about.body:
Berlin 2026 is an independent project comparing party programs across policy areas ahead of the 2026 Berlin state election. Official programs are published only in German — we translate them into languages spoken in Berlin.

Nina compares the programs and develops the project; Masha handles the technical side. In parallel we work on [Water for All / Wasser für alle](https://www.water4all.com.de) — an open atlas of free drinking water in Berlin. The project makes access to water visible and helps residents push for new drinking fountains.
about.contributeBody:
If you’d like to support the project, the most useful thing you can do is spread the word — share it with people who might find it helpful.

And if you spot a mistake on the site — wrong wording or a factual slip — please tell us so we can fix it. Select the passage on the page to open a report, or write to us via Contact.

aiDisclosure.title: AI Disclosure
aiDisclosure.intro: This page explains how we use artificial intelligence (AI) tools when creating content for this website, and how human editors remain responsible for what we publish.
aiDisclosure.howWeUseAiContent: We use AI tools to help draft and refine website text — for example, page copy and summaries of official party election programs. AI assists with wording, structure, and extracting comparable positions; it does not decide what we publish or how you should vote.
aiDisclosure.humanResponsibilityContent: All ideas, goals, and substantive decisions behind this website come from people working on the Berlin 2026 project. Before anything is published, content is reviewed for clarity and fit with the project’s informational purpose. Editorial responsibility for this website lies with the Berlin 2026 project.
aiDisclosure.reviewAndAccuracyContent: The party comparison table is compiled with substantial AI assistance from official party programs. We recommend double-checking points that matter to you. Full translations of the main parties’ programs are published on BerlinVote.Help. We check content for accuracy, but errors can still occur and some nuance may be missed. If you spot a mistake, please let us know.
aiDisclosure.contactContent: Questions about how we use AI or about the content on this site? Write to us at nina.harz@pm.me.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: This privacy policy explains how we collect, use, and protect your personal information when you visit our website, in compliance with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and applicable German data protection law (including the TTDSG).
privacy.dataProcessedContent:
When you visit our website, our hosting provider may automatically process technical data required to deliver the site (for example IP address, browser/user-agent information, and request timestamps in server logs). We do not operate user accounts or require registration.

If you use the optional feedback form, we process your message, the page URL, the interface language, and — if you choose to provide it — your email address so we can reply.

If you report incorrect wording or a factual mistake (including via the “Report this text” control after selecting text), we process the quoted incorrect text, your suggested correction, the page URL, and the interface language.

When you submit either form, we also process a Cloudflare Turnstile security token and related technical signals needed to verify that the request is not automated spam.
privacy.hostingContent: This website is hosted by Vercel Inc. Server infrastructure and content delivery may involve processing outside the European Economic Area under appropriate safeguards (including Standard Contractual Clauses where applicable). See [Vercel’s Privacy Policy](https://vercel.com/legal/privacy-policy).
privacy.processorsContent:
We use the following service providers as processors (Art. 28 GDPR) for the purposes described below. Transfers to the United States may occur; we rely on appropriate safeguards such as Standard Contractual Clauses and the providers’ data processing terms.

• Vercel Inc. — hosting and delivery of the website.
• Cloudflare, Inc. — Cloudflare Turnstile bot/spam protection when a feedback or text-report form is opened or submitted. Turnstile may process IP address and browser/device characteristics to issue a verification token. Details: [Cloudflare Privacy Policy](https://www.cloudflare.com/privacypolicy/) and Turnstile documentation.
• Resend, Inc. — transactional email delivery of submitted feedback and text reports to us. Details: [Resend Privacy Policy](https://resend.com/legal/privacy-policy).

Legal basis for Turnstile and related security measures: Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR (legitimate interest in protecting the forms against abuse and spam). Where the user requests the form service, storage of or access to information on the end device that is strictly necessary for that service may also be covered by § 25(2) TTDSG.
privacy.purposeOfProcessingContent:
We process data to:

• Provide, secure, and maintain this website (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR)
• Receive and handle optional feedback and text/factual-error reports (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR)
• Reply when you voluntarily provide an email address (Art. 6(1)(a) GDPR and/or Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR, depending on the request)
• Prevent spam and automated abuse of the forms via Turnstile (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR)
privacy.retentionContent:
Server logs are retained by the hosting provider only as long as needed for security and operations, then deleted or anonymised according to the provider’s practices.

Feedback and text-report messages (including any email you provide) are kept only as long as necessary to review and handle your submission, and for a short period thereafter if needed for follow-up or documentation, then deleted.

Turnstile verification tokens are used for the security check and are not stored by us as a long-term profile.
privacy.cookiesContent:
This website does not use analytics or advertising cookies.

A language preference may be stored in a small cookie or in local storage so we can show your chosen language on return visits.

Cloudflare Turnstile may set or read technical cookies or similar storage only when you open or use a feedback/report form, for bot protection. We do not use Turnstile for advertising or cross-site tracking.

You can delete cookies and site data in your browser settings at any time.
privacy.yourRightsIntro: Under the GDPR, you have the following rights regarding your personal data:
privacy.yourRightsList:
• Right of access (Art. 15 GDPR)
• Right to rectification (Art. 16 GDPR)
• Right to erasure (Art. 17 GDPR)
• Right to restriction of processing (Art. 18 GDPR)
• Right to data portability (Art. 20 GDPR)
• Right to object to processing based on legitimate interests (Art. 21 GDPR)
• Right to withdraw consent where processing is based on consent (Art. 7(3) GDPR)
• Right to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority (Art. 77 GDPR)
privacy.supervisoryAuthorityContent:
You may lodge a complaint with a data protection supervisory authority. For Berlin, this is typically:

Berliner Beauftragte für Datenschutz und Informationsfreiheit
Alt-Moabit 59–61, 10555 Berlin, Germany
[https://www.datenschutz-berlin.de](https://www.datenschutz-berlin.de)
privacy.contactInfo: To exercise your rights or ask questions about your data, contact us at nina.harz@pm.me.
